catalysts.headline: Coverage of Oracle's AI-datacenter financing needs: company said it expects to raise roughly $40 billion in debt and equity in fiscal 2027 (having already raised $43B debt + $5B equity in FY2026); FY2026 capex rose to $55.7B from $21.2B in FY2025, and FY2027 capex guidance is $90-95B; FY2026 free cash flow was reported as negative $23.7B
catalysts.note: Secondary reporting on Oracle's FY2026 10-K disclosures; not independently fetched from the primary filing this session (SEC EDGAR unreachable).

catalysts.headline: Upcoming ex-dividend date for Oracle's regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.50/share (payable 2026-10-23); routine, part of the dividend program already in place, not a new declaration

Oracle fell ~4.7%-4.85% amid a broad AI-linked stock selloff, triggered by weekend comments from Anthropic and OpenAI leadership (including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, in a 2026-09-11 Fortune interview) urging a slower pace of frontier AI development and confirming OpenAI's IPO will not occur in 2026 (pushed to 2027 or later); compounded by ongoing concern over Oracle's debt-funded AI capex buildout (Q1 FY2027 capex $28.5B vs $8.5B a year earlier; FY2027 capex guidance maintained at $90B-$95B)
catalysts.impact: -4.7% to -4.85% on the day per multiple outlets

catalysts.headline: Oracle publicly rejected a Bloomberg report claiming certain OpenAI-committed data centers would slip to 2028 (a one-year delay from original schedule), stating 'There have been no delays on the sites required to meet our contractual commitments' and that timelines were jointly validated with OpenAI

Executive Chair/CTO Larry Ellison cancelled his Rule 10b5-1 trading plan (adopted 2026-06-22) that would have allowed sale of up to 50 million Oracle shares (~$7.5B); no shares were sold under the plan prior to cancellation; company gave no explanation, and Ellison stated he has no other plans to sell Oracle stock
catalysts.impact: cited by multiple outlets as a contributing factor in 2026-09-14 trading alongside the broader AI-sector selloff

catalysts.headline: Oracle disclosed (in a regulatory filing following its Q1 FY2027 close) that it is expanding its 2026 Restructuring Plan by approximately $700M, raising total estimated plan costs to roughly $2.8B (severance, contract termination, and related exit costs tied in part to AI-driven workforce reductions); ~$2.1B in charges had been recorded against the plan through 2026-08-31
catalysts.impact: cited as a contributing factor in the stock's decline

catalysts.headline: FY2026 remaining performance obligations (RPO) reached $638B; disclosed $248B in additional off-balance-sheet lease commitments (15-19 year terms, 'substantially all related to data centers and cloud capacity'); disclosed $75B of customer-prepaid/supplied hardware reducing Oracle's own GPU capex burden
catalysts.note: Secondary reporting on the FY2026 10-K; exact filing date not pinned down (annual report would have been filed mid-2026) and not independently fetched this session.

pendingFilings.note: Las Vegas; expected to detail long-term AI-infrastructure capex plans per preview coverage (Morningstar). Has not yet occurred as of this report (2026-10-22).

notes: Theme on file ('Advanced Materials') is a clear mismatch -- Oracle is an enterprise software / database / cloud-infrastructure company, not a materials company. Reassigned theme to 'Enterprise Software & Security' (the closest genuine fit among the existing theme strings); 'AI Semiconductors' was considered but rejected because Oracle does not design or manufacture chips -- it is a large buyer/consumer of AI compute and a cloud provider, which is a materially different business model. themeLabel set to 'hot sector' given the scale of current AI-datacenter capex/financing news driving the stock narrative, despite Oracle being a long-established company. The 93% OCI growth figure and the FY2026 capex/RPO/lease figures above are the most substantive items this session could establish and should be cross-checked against Oracle's actual 10-K/earnings release in a follow-up pass.
